files.why: Add the snake_case server DTO schema for the per-customer reschedule flag response (DTOs must stay in data/).
Map the flag DTO into a plain core boolean so the DTO never leaks upward.
Add fetchRescheduleEnabled(clientId) that reads the flag via httpTransport, mirroring the existing query pattern.
Add an MSW handler serving the per-customer flag — the concrete 'flip without deploying' point in this mock-API repo.
Thread an injected 'enabled' boolean through canReschedule/validateReschedule so the disabled case is a pure, message-bearing domain rule.
Accept the flag and pass it to validateReschedule so submit is gated and surfaces the domain message.
Load per-client reschedule availability for the day's appointments so the view can gate the button.
Show/hide the Reschedule button per appointment based on its customer's flag.
Cover the new policy gate: reschedule denied when the customer flag is off, allowed when on.
Test the new flag DTO→core mapper, mirroring the existing billing.mappers.test.ts.

uncertain: Whether the flag gate belongs in core/policy.ts (pure boolean injected, chosen here so the 'unavailable' message lives in the domain) or should be UI-only capability gating with core left untouched — both are defensible under the constitution.

Whether to extend useDaySchedule for availability vs. add a dedicated ui/composables/useRescheduleAvailability.ts; I folded it into the existing loader since DayView is the only consumer, but a separate composable is cleaner if reused (rules 6/7).

A generic flag-fetch mechanism could theoretically go in shared/http or shared/lib, but only one slice uses it and 'reschedule' is a domain noun, so per rule 7 it stays inside scheduling (duplicate later, promote at the 3rd same-reason use).
Whether index.ts needs changes: I left it untouched because the reschedule flow is scheduling's own UI and no other slice/app reads the flag — but that assumes no cross-slice consumer needs it.
questions: What does 'customer' mean here — the end-client on an appointment (clientId, e.g. c-ana) or the SaaS tenant/account using Vise? The keying and endpoint shape depend on this.

Where should the flag be sourced: a dedicated feature-flag endpoint (e.g. /api/feature-flags?client=), a field on an existing client/appointment payload, or an external flag service? This decides the DTO/query design.
Is UI gating sufficient, or must the reschedule mutation (PATCH /api/appointments/:id) also be rejected server-side when the flag is off? Hiding the button alone doesn't stop a direct API call.
Caching/freshness expectations: is a fetch-on-load flag acceptable, or does 'without deploying' imply near-real-time propagation (polling/invalidation) after an operator flips it?
Should turning the flow off apply only to new reschedules, or also hide/disable an already-open reschedule form and in-progress edits?
